newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude markets pick up on healthy demand.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude markets pick up on healthy demand.

text.p: North Sea crude markets saw a flurry of activity on Thursday, with differentials firming and most first decade July cargoes already snapped up, traders said.
Heavy end-user requirements and uncertainty over when Iraq would resume its crude exports lent the market a firmer tone, with many buyers switching their attention to the second decade of July.
"There is precious little left in any grade for the first 10 days so if you want barrels you're going to have to pay solid numbers," said one trader.
Paper markets firmed slightly as well, but were overshadowed by the physical activity.
An Ekofisk loading July 7-9 traded at dated Brent +20 cents, a slightly firmer number than on Wednesday, while an Oseberg cargo for July 14-16 was done at dated +14 cents, dealers said.
Another Ekofisk, loading July 9-11, was believed traded at dated +20 cents but the seller would not immediately confirm the deal. A third Ekofisk was also rumoured to have changed hands.
Amid rumours of a number of private deals a Gullfaks A loading July 8-10 was confirmed to have gone for dated Brent -3 cents while an end-June Troll cargo was heard traded for "positive numbers."
"We've had improving differentials and good demand," said one seller. "We have no Oseberg left for the first 11 days of July and almost no Statfjord either for the first decade."
Other grades were also firmer with a Statfjord loading July 17-19 traded on Wednesday at dated +33 cents, three cents more than the previous deal, which was done for earlier loading material.
